name: Example: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization
problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/45cefb7311cd5253b76164cc7f2f3ce01b445f0e9061b720865227128b60debe.png)
If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 \cdot y_2?$
worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/b521c0b31d05de273d0abd37e00b046c0e36ed47ef30d22784a24cace4d676f9.png)

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/9dcc9f71745cce72ce7e122b3bc8cd7064d05f3be90d712202f42956956ef18e.png)
This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=6 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $y_1=6$ and $y_2=4.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/903fbfe6828526dace264d65baebf58c31e36db8a54e25ed1f3be859e6079ebb.png)

- Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/dcb234ae13cab2676ea5afa7fde452c870ff5088ff5748342c517bf2a96327a8.png)
This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $x_2=-2$ and $x_1=2.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/53bace542ba4dfd0d7e5e4bf9b6451c7f39502dd1bf24d030f654050629f0e0d.png)

Finally, $x_1 \cdot y_2 = 2 \cdot 4 = 8.$
